newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open firmer after Dow unaffected by Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open firmer after Dow unaffected by Greenspan.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Wednesday, the market recovering most of Tuesday's decline after an address to a U.S. senate committee by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan failed to disturb U.S. markets.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.4 points firmer at 2,440.7.
Resources issues were leading the recovery after being worst affected by selling on Tuesday. Bellwether stock BHP opened modestly firmer.

"The market hasn't rushed ahead this morning. It's reasonably steady at the moment but I wouldn't be surprised to see it come off on a bit of profit-taking later this afternoon," said Jim Tredenick, a dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Nevitts.

Tredenick said early market interest was focused on Western Australian gold producer Mt Edon Gold Mines, whose shares spiked up after a parcel totalling about 10 percent of its issued capital was put through the market.
The industrial sector opened slightly higher with beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil and finance and property group Lend Lease the most sought after of the industrials.
At 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), Coca-Cola Amatil shares were 26 cents higher at A$13.26 (US$10.34) while Lend Lease shares were 43 cents up at A$23.60.
